jurisdiction.venue: Sofia City Court & European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO)

headline: Company Declared Insolvent in 2012 Helped Win €213.7 Million E.U. Railway Grant Seven Years Later, Prosecutors Allege
deck: The European Public Prosecutor’s Office indicted a corporate representative at the Sofia City Court after Bulgaria’s rail authority paid €68.2 million to a consortium for Sofia–Plovdiv track upgrades. The defendant is presumed innocent.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: EPPO indicted a consortium company representative at Sofia City Court over an allegedly false solvency declaration used to secure a €213.7M (~$232M) EU railway grant with €68.2M disbursed; defendant presumed innocent.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: If proven, the allegations would resemble certifying zero bankruptcies on a €5,000 municipal small-business grant seven years after filing for insolvency
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Routine automated registry rejection before a single euro leaves the treasury

sources.title: Bulgaria: EPPO indicts individual in €213.7 million fraud investigation involving the modernisation of the railway infrastructure

interactive_art_spec.caption: A Bulgarian State Railways electric locomotive on the national network. European prosecutors filed an indictment in Sofia over an alleged false solvency declaration tied to a €213.7 million Sofia–Plovdiv rail modernization grant.
